newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hamanaka trial raises question of S"tomo controls.
newsitem.headline: Hamanaka trial raises question of S"tomo controls.

text.p: The trial of Sumitomo Corp"s former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka looks set to spotlight the nagging issue of lax checks and controls at Japan"s top corporations and financial institutions.

A lawyer for Hamanaka, who on Monday pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery charges in connection with the trade house"s massive copper market losses, said the defense plans to call an official from Sumitomo"s credit control division to the stand at the next hearing on March 10.
"It will allow us to hear directly what the system of checks at Sumitomo headquarters was like," Hamanaka lawyer Hidesato Sekine told reporters.

Prosecutors on Monday said Hamanaka resorted to fraud and forgery in order to deceive his superiors about a massive copper trading loss, eventually estimated at $2.6 billion, that he amassed over 10 years of unnauthorised deals.
Sumitomo has repeatedly insisted that Hamanaka"s superiors knew nothing of his off-the-books trading.
Many traders have expressed astonishment, however, that higher-ups at the trading giant could be kept in the dark for so long about such huge losses.
"This would generally be unthinkable at a Japanese trade house," said one trader at a major Sumitomo rival.
Prosecutors said, however, that Hamanaka gained the full trust of his superiors by creating the appearance that the copper team was consistently generating a profit and that he was a talented dealer.
They said he did this to discourage them from transferring him to a different division, in which case his losses would have been exposed.

Prosecutors also said he doctored balance statements from counterparties to Sumitomo"s copper transactions, and when Sumitomo set up a team in 1992 to check statements from each counterparty, Hamanaka was made head of the team and prevented its other members from contacting counterparties directly.
